name: Skeena26

pitch_detail.notes: Find the narrow whale's-back rib between two facing corners; the nine bolts are hard to see in the shade. A bouldery 5.9 move gains the rib, then 5.7-5.8 friction leads to polished rock near the top with a few more 5.9 moves. Step onto a flake on the left, place gear in good cracks just above, then traverse right to the belay ledge.

The character of most of the route: friction on brilliant white granite covered in knobs and bumps, mostly 5.4-5.6. Bolts are spaced roughly 10-20 feet apart and hard to spot in shade, so look ahead before leaving each anchor.
More knobbed slab at 5.6 with occasional 5.8 moves. On rappel, 60 m ropes let these two pitches be combined into one rappel.
A 5.8 section starts on this pitch, and it can carry running water even when the rest of the route is dry. Be ready for wet smears on this pitch.
There is a gear crack on this pitch that is easy to miss; climbing past it turns the pitch into a long runout. Look for it before running it out.

Climb up and right past four bolts (nothing harder than 5.7), then finish on clean 5.7 splitter cracks and a few face moves past the left side of an overhang, onto the forested ledge on top of the buttress with views of Whitehorse Mountain. The wall's true summit is further up brushy scrambling.

rappels: 12 rappels on two 50 m ropes down the line of ascent, one per pitch; with 60 m ropes, pitches 5 and 6 combine for 11
descent_text: Rappel the line of ascent; 50-meter ropes are adequate for most pitches, while 60-meter ropes allow combining pitches 5 and 6 to speed the descent.
approach: South Face is another wall within the same Squire Creek Walls complex as Waterfall Basin, reached via the same Darrington-area approach: I-5 to the Arlington exit, SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington, then Squire Creek Road to the washout-blocked parking area. From there, follow the rough, unmaintained climbers' approach — the old roadbed past a landslide crossing to a boot track that drops to a ford of Squire Creek, then a climbers' track across a tributary and up through old-growth forest into two steep, dirty gullies that top out on the grassy saddle below the South Face, roughly 3 hours from the car, with route-finding (flagging, cairns) required in several spots.
overview: A 12-pitch, 1,500-ft friction climb on immaculate, knobby grey granite, with a polished 5.9 crux on pitch one easing into mostly 5.4-5.6 climbing above, finishing on clean splitter cracks overlooking Whitehorse Mountain.
beta: Pitch 1 climbs a narrow 'whale's back' of stone between facing corners on polished friction, protected by nine bolts, and holds the route's crux. Subsequent pitches ease to 5.4-5.6 with occasional 5.8 sections. The final pitch features clean splitter cracks (5.7) finishing on the buttress crest with views over Whitehorse Mountain.
fa: David Whitelaw, Bill Enger, and Yale Lewis, September 17, 2012
